subject: AcmeHealth — GDPR / DPA & SCC follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thompson <alice@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth kickoff — GDPR / security follow-up

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood is currently in SOC 2 Type II audit period; expected issuance Q4 2026. We can share interim control documentation and the last Type I summary on request.

2) GDPR / DPA: You asked for a DPA template we use. I'm attaching our standard Redwood_DPA_v1.pdf. Happy to start with that and accept redlines from your legal team.

3) SCCs: Given AcmeHealth will act as Controller and Redwood as Processor (please confirm below), the applicable SCC module is the Controller-to-Processor module. I've attached a short SCC_matrix.xlsx that maps which clauses we expect to apply.

4) Vendor security questionnaire: thanks for sending the questionnaire during the call — I've attached the version we received (vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf). We'll start filling the high-priority items (security posture, encryption, data residency). Expect first pass by end of week.

Proposed next steps: 
- Can you confirm AcmeHealth's role (Controller) and that Redwood will be Processor for the services in scope?
- I’ll circulate the DPA via DocuSign and copy your legal contact. If you prefer we can provide a redline instead.
- Marissa (legal) and Rishi (solutions) are looped for any technical / contractual clarifications.

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v1.pdf, SCC_matrix.xlsx

Thanks — happy to sync again next week if helpful.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | (555) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform
From: Alice Thompson <alice@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Jenkins <bob.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 17:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth kickoff — GDPR / security follow-up

Hi Neha — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. Confirming the following from AcmeHealth's side: 

- AcmeHealth will be the Controller for patient data and PHI flows. Redwood will be acting as Processor for the inference API and hosted embeddings service in scope.
- We would like to see your preferred Controller-to-Processor DPA and would appreciate a DocuSign link to speed review.
- Regarding SCCs: our privacy team typically expects the EU Commission Controller-to-Processor module (Module 2) — please confirm your mapping in the SCC_matrix.xlsx.

Timeline: our legal team can do an initial pass next Tuesday (21 Jul). If you can send the DPA and any recommended SCC module selections today or Monday, we'll start review and share redlines.

One question — does Redwood already accept the Controller-to-Processor SCCs as-is, or do you typically negotiate narrow redlines for clauses on sub-processing and audit rights?

Appreciate the help — copying Bob (technical lead) for any follow-ups on the questionnaire answers.

Best,
Alice Thompson
Head of Privacy & Compliance | AcmeHealth
alice@acmehealth.com | +44 20 7946 0623
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thompson <alice@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth kickoff — GDPR / security follow-up

Hi Alice — great, thanks for confirming role alignment. Short answers below and next actions: 

- Controller/Processor: confirmed — AcmeHealth = Controller; Redwood = Processor. We'll include that explicitly in the DPA.

- SCC module: we recommend applying the EU Commission Controller-to-Processor module (Module 2) for the data flows you described. SCC_matrix.xlsx includes our recommended mapping and a short note on where we request narrow clarifications (primarily on subprocessor notification timelines and audit scope).

- Negotiation approach: Redwood's standard position is to accept the Controller-to-Processor SCCs. We are open to limited redlines around subprocessor onboarding notice (we ask for 10 days minimum) and mutually agreed audit windows. Anything substantive from your legal team, Marissa will handle.

DPA delivery: I’ve created the DPA in DocuSign so your legal team can review and sign or start redlines. Link: https://docusign.net/Neha/Redwood_DPA_v1 (DocuSign envelope created).

Questionnaire & SOC2: Rishi is starting the first-pass answers to the vendor questionnaire and expects to share the draft by EOD Wednesday 22 Jul. For SOC 2, we can provide control narratives and a SOC 2 Type I summary now; Type II expected in Q4 2026.

Next steps: 
- We’ll upload the completed questionnaire draft to the Drive folder and share link.
- Marissa, can you please confirm whether Redwood can accept Module 2 as-is or if legal anticipates any redlines?

Thanks — Neha

Attachments: none (DPA via DocuSign link)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thompson <alice@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth kickoff — GDPR / security follow-up

Hi Alice — thanks for looping us in. I’m Marissa from Redwood Legal — copying Rishi for any technical clarifications. Quick note from legal review: 

- We can accept the EU Controller-to-Processor (Module 2) SCCs as the baseline. If AcmeHealth provides redlines, we’ll review and aim to keep changes minimal.

- We are generally flexible on subprocessor notification windows; our standard is 10 business days prior notice (we accept requests to shorten to 5 business days on a case-by-case basis for high-priority subprocessors).

- For audit rights: we typically provide a combination of report-based and on-site audit options. For on-site audits we favor a mutually agreed schedule and scoped to the specific controls in question.

I’ve attached a redline of the DPA (DPA_redline_acme.pdf) showing the limited contractual clarifications we’d propose if Acme’s legal team wants to see suggested language up front.

Proposed meeting: I’m available Tuesday 27 Jul at 10:00 AM BST for a short legal sync to walk through any items. If that works for your team, let us know and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (555) 555-0199
